decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Advanced Bioinformatics
decks.description: Infer biological structure and function from high-dimensional molecular evidence.

includes: Single-cell and multi-omics inference, sequence models, structural interpretation and validation
excludes: Every omics technology and de novo protein-folding algorithm

practice: Complete a multi-omics reanalysis and a sequence-model implementation, separating computational confidence from experimental validation of biological mechanism.

outcomes.description: Implement a sequence hidden-Markov model with forward/backward inference; use documented protein-structure and interaction tools with confidence/coordinate interpretation and validate functional hypotheses against independent experiments and leakage-aware benchmarks.

Construct count-based and latent-variable models for bulk/single-cell molecular data, account for batch and missingness and integrate expression, accessibility and sequence evidence without conflating clusters with cell identities.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biological Laboratory Methods
decks.description: Generate reproducible biological evidence.

includes: Microscopy, sterile handling, pipetting, molecular assays and biological study design

practice: Run or analyze a supervised nonpathogenic culture and PCR investigation with positive/negative controls, contamination checks and a preregistered analysis.

outcomes.description: Perform dilution, sterile transfer, basic nonpathogenic culture, microscopy, DNA extraction, PCR and gel electrophoresis; explain each assay's physical representation, controls and failure modes.
Design replicated, randomized and blinded experiments; distinguish technical from biological replication and justify consent, organism welfare, biosafety and data-provenance decisions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Cell Biology
decks.description: Explain cellular organization and interpret cell-level evidence.

includes: Membranes, organelles, cytoskeleton, cell cycle and cellular observation
excludes: Detailed metabolic pathways and research-grade imaging

practice: Annotate and quantify a microscopy image set, then distinguish altered localization, cell number and imaging artifact as explanations.

outcomes.description: Explain membrane transport, compartmentation, trafficking, cytoskeletal movement, cell division and receptor signaling using molecular interaction and concentration-gradient models.
Interpret light and fluorescence images with scale bars, controls and resolution limits; quantify cell size, localization and division counts from provided images.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Cellular and Developmental Research
decks.description: Design mechanistic cellular and developmental investigations.

includes: Quantitative imaging, signaling dynamics, cell-fate research and causal perturbations

practice: Reanalyze a live-cell dataset and propose a factorial perturbation study with quantified competing predictions, negative controls and a reproducible image-analysis audit.

outcomes.description: Integrate timed genetic perturbations, rescue, live imaging and molecular readouts to discriminate signaling, mechanical and cell-fate mechanisms; justify model-organism choice and welfare or consent tradeoffs.

Use documented segmentation and tracking tools after teaching thresholding, connected components and assignment procedures; quantify cell trajectories, localization and lineage transitions with artifact and uncertainty checks.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Computational Neuroscience
decks.description: Model neural dynamics and infer neural representations.

includes: Conductance models, neural networks, spike-process models and neural coding

practice: Implement a conductance-based circuit and fit a spike-encoding model, comparing dynamical mechanism, predictive fit and intervention evidence.

outcomes.description: Derive a conditional-intensity point-process likelihood from time-bin probabilities, fit encoding/decoding models and compare information measures and held-out predictions under stimulus and intervention controls.

Derive conductance-based membrane and gating equations, implement single-neuron and coupled excitatory/inhibitory networks and analyze equilibria, excitability, oscillations and explicit plasticity rules.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Conservation Biology
decks.description: Translate ecological evidence into defensible conservation action.

includes: Biodiversity assessment, habitat change, restoration and conservation decisions

practice: Use a provided GIS viewer and monitoring data to propose a reserve/restoration plan with an adaptive monitoring and decision protocol.

outcomes.description: Assess extinction pressures, habitat fragmentation, invasive species and climate exposure using abundance, occupancy and mapped habitat data with explicit detection and scale limitations.
Compare protection, restoration and harvest interventions using measurable objectives, uncertainty, costs, Indigenous/local knowledge and competing stakeholder obligations.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Developmental Biology
decks.description: Infer how genes and cell interactions construct organisms.

includes: Embryogenesis, patterning, differentiation, morphogenesis and regeneration

practice: Reconstruct a developmental mechanism from spatial images and perturbations and propose a decisive lineage or rescue experiment.

outcomes.description: Interpret lineage tracing, transplantation, mosaic and loss/gain-of-function evidence; design controlled tests distinguishing cell autonomy, competence and instructive signaling.
Explain axis formation, induction, morphogen thresholds, cell-fate specification and tissue movement using lineage and spatial gene-expression representations across animal and plant examples.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Ecological and Evolutionary Research
decks.description: Connect ecological and evolutionary theory to imperfect field evidence.

includes: Eco-evolutionary feedback, spatial discrete models, hierarchical field inference and research design
excludes: All spatial stochastic-process and diffusion-limit theories

practice: Fit an integrated population model, compare competing spatial or evolutionary mechanisms and defend a feasible, ethically justified field-research design.

outcomes.description: Derive invasion-fitness and coupled trait/population models and implement spatial patch and individual-based stochastic models; compare deterministic and stochastic predictions and assess scale dependence.

Construct hierarchical models integrating demographic, environmental and genetic observations; evaluate posterior predictive adequacy and design monitoring or experiments that distinguish eco-evolutionary mechanisms.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Ecology and Evolution
decks.description: Use population and environmental evidence to explain biological patterns.

includes: Population and community ecology, ecosystems, selection and macroevolution

practice: Analyze a field-sampling dataset and a trait-frequency time series, explicitly checking detection and alternative evolutionary explanations.

outcomes.description: Calculate discrete population growth, energy and nutrient budgets and simple diversity measures; estimate abundance from quadrat and mark-recapture data under stated assumptions.
Compare selection, drift, gene flow, speciation and historical explanations using trait, fossil and environmental evidence; separate ecological association from causal effect.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Epidemiology
decks.description: Infer population-health patterns and evaluate interventions.

includes: Epidemiological designs, risk measures, causal bias and discrete transmission models
excludes: Clinical treatment and continuous-time epidemic theory

practice: Evaluate a screening study and a synthetic outbreak, auditing causal claims and recommending an intervention with explicit equity tradeoffs.

outcomes.description: Calculate incidence, prevalence, risk and odds ratios; compare cohort, case-control and trial evidence using explicit confounding, selection and measurement-bias diagrams.

Construct a spreadsheet susceptible-infectious-recovered recurrence with stated contact and recovery probabilities; compare screening or prevention policies using uncertainty, privacy and distributional consequences.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Evolutionary Genetics
decks.description: Infer evolutionary processes from genetic variation.

includes: Selection, drift, migration, coalescence and phylogenetic inference

practice: Implement a population simulator and a small-tree likelihood calculation, then compare competing historical explanations for a genetic dataset.

outcomes.description: Construct character and sequence trees using parsimony and a locally specified finite-state substitution likelihood with pruning; compare bootstrap support, homoplasy and model sensitivity.

Derive discrete allele-frequency recurrences and implement Wright-Fisher sampling, mutation, migration and selection; calculate heterozygosity, linkage disequilibrium and simple coalescent waiting probabilities.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Genetics
decks.description: Infer inheritance patterns and gene relationships.

includes: Meiosis, Mendelian and non-Mendelian inheritance, linkage and genetic evidence

practice: Analyze a blinded set of crosses and pedigrees and defend both a genetic model and limits on individual prediction.

outcomes.description: Use mutation, complementation and segregation evidence to distinguish gene function, allelic relationships and environmental effects while evaluating genetic privacy and deterministic claims.
Predict genotype and phenotype probabilities for pedigrees and crosses, including linkage, sex linkage, epistasis and cytoplasmic inheritance; estimate recombination maps.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Genomics
decks.description: Reconstruct and interrogate genomes computationally.

includes: Sequencing data models, alignment, assembly, variant analysis and genomic testing
excludes: Wet-lab library preparation and advanced multi-omics

practice: Analyze a public or synthetic read dataset with provenance and privacy controls, verifying selected calls against simulated ground truth.

outcomes.description: Explain how sequencing generates reads and quality scores; implement dynamic-programming alignment and a small de Bruijn assembly and interpret mapping, repeats and coverage limitations.

Construct a reproducible quality-control, variant and expression-count workflow using documented tools; calculate genotype likelihoods under a taught read-error model and control false discoveries in genomic comparisons.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Immunology
decks.description: Explain immune responses and interpret immune evidence.

includes: Innate/adaptive immunity, tolerance, vaccination and immune assays

practice: Analyze a multigroup immune-assay dataset, construct control-aware gates and defend a limited claim about a vaccine response.

outcomes.description: Interpret ELISA, flow-cytometry gates and vaccination data using explicitly taught assay signals, controls and denominators; distinguish immune correlates from demonstrated protection.
Trace antigen recognition, presentation, lymphocyte activation, receptor diversification, effector responses, memory and tolerance and explain allergy, autoimmunity and immune evasion.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Living Systems
decks.description: Reason about living systems across scales.

includes: Cells, organisms, inheritance, evolution and biological evidence

practice: Compare unfamiliar organisms from images and observations; propose and critique competing explanations for a growth experiment.

outcomes.description: Distinguish observation from mechanism, compare evolutionary explanations and design a controlled comparison with measurable biological variables.
Represent cellular organization, major biomolecule roles, energy and matter exchange, DNA inheritance and organism-environment relationships using labeled diagrams.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Microbiology
decks.description: Investigate microorganisms as organisms and interacting communities.

includes: Microbial metabolism, growth, viruses, ecology and identification

practice: Investigate a nonpathogenic isolate or curated case dataset with a decision tree of orthogonal tests and a contamination-control plan.

outcomes.description: Compare bacterial, archaeal, fungal and viral replication, metabolic strategies, gene exchange and host/environment interactions; calculate growth and viable counts from dilution data.
Use culture, staining, biochemical, susceptibility and sequence-assay evidence to identify microbes and distinguish resistance, contamination, colonization and causal infection.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Molecular Genetics
decks.description: Explain and experimentally interrogate gene expression and genome maintenance.

includes: Replication, repair, expression, chromatin and molecular genetic intervention

practice: Design and, where authorized, execute a benign reporter perturbation with sequence-verified constructs, normalized measurements and a rescue test.

outcomes.description: Trace replication, repair, recombination, transcription, RNA processing, translation and chromatin regulation; predict molecular consequences of sequence and regulatory perturbations.

Design cloning, reporter, quantitative-PCR, genome-editing and rescue experiments using explicit construct maps, guide/primer constraints and controls; distinguish off-target, dosage and regulatory effects.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Neuroscience
decks.description: Connect cellular neural signals to circuit and behavioral function.

includes: Neural signaling, sensory/motor systems, plasticity and neural evidence

practice: Analyze spike and behavioral recordings and compare a passive membrane model with observations, explicitly identifying where active-channel mechanisms are needed.

outcomes.description: Use locally defined Nernst potentials, RC membrane response and threshold/reset models to calculate bounded neuronal responses; explain action potentials, synaptic transmission and plasticity without claiming full conductance dynamics.
Relate sensory, motor, autonomic and memory circuits to anatomy and behavior; quantify spike histograms and receptive fields and evaluate recording, lesion and intervention evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Organismal Diversity
decks.description: Interpret biological diversity through comparative structure and ancestry.

includes: Major lineages, comparative anatomy, life cycles and organismal adaptations

practice: Build an illustrated comparative specimen portfolio and defend a character matrix and tree against alternative character codings.

outcomes.description: Classify representative bacteria, archaea, protists, fungi, plants and animals using diagnostic characters and construct a small character-based phylogenetic hypothesis.
Compare body plans, reproductive cycles, nutrition and environmental adaptations, distinguishing homology, convergence and functional constraint.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Physiology
decks.description: Explain integrated organismal function through transport and feedback.

includes: Animal organ systems, homeostasis, plant transport and environmental regulation
excludes: Clinical diagnosis and detailed neural computation

practice: Interpret perturbation time courses from animal homeostasis and plant gas exchange, using explicit compartment diagrams and mass balances.

outcomes.description: Analyze animal cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, digestive, endocrine, muscular and reproductive function using mass balance, pressure-flow, diffusion, receptor occupancy and negative-feedback models taught with their assumptions.

Explain plant water potential, xylem/phloem transport, mineral nutrition, stomatal regulation, photosynthetic exchange and hormonal responses; calculate bounded transport and water-balance predictions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Quantitative Ecology
decks.description: Predict ecological dynamics and estimate hidden ecological states.

includes: Population interactions, structured populations, observation models and ecological estimation

practice: Estimate a population trend with imperfect detection and compare competing dynamic models using held-out surveys and sensitivity analysis.

outcomes.description: Construct and analyze logistic, consumer-resource, competition and age/stage-matrix models, calculating equilibria, stability, growth rates and sensitivity.

Fit abundance, occupancy and capture-recapture models using explicitly constructed detection likelihoods and documented optimizers; distinguish process/observation error and assess identifiability and out-of-sample prediction.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Systems Biology
decks.description: Construct and test mechanistic models of biological networks.

includes: Biochemical networks, metabolic flux, dynamic regulation and system identification

practice: Implement a regulatory-network ODE model, fit a perturbation time course and propose a new measurement that resolves a demonstrated parameter ambiguity.

outcomes.description: Construct stoichiometric matrices and mass-action/enzyme-rate ODEs for metabolism and gene regulation; analyze conservation, steady flux null spaces, feedback, bistability and oscillation.

Estimate dynamic parameters using documented optimizers, implement sensitivity equations and profile-likelihood checks and design perturbations that distinguish structurally or practically unidentifiable models.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Advanced Synthesis
decks.description: Design and substantiate multistep molecular syntheses.

includes: Stereoselective synthesis, pericyclic reactions, catalytic transformations and route validation

practice: Defend two competing routes to a complex target and execute or critically reconstruct a supervised short sequence with identity, purity and waste evidence.

outcomes.description: Plan convergent multistep routes using stereoselective carbon-carbon construction, locally taught frontier-orbital/pericyclic selection rules and organocatalytic or metal-catalyzed transformations.

Compare mechanistic and spectral evidence for product identity and selectivity; optimize a bounded synthesis using controls, mass balance and kinetic evidence and justify safety and sustainability tradeoffs.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Analytical Chemistry
decks.description: Determine chemical composition from calibrated measurements.

includes: Calibration, titrimetry, gravimetry, chromatography, optical and mass-based quantification

practice: Analyze an unknown mixture using two techniques and reconcile calibration, spike recovery, detection limits and disagreement between methods.

outcomes.description: Use Beer-Lambert absorption, chromatographic retention/resolution and mass-to-charge separation models to quantify mixtures; diagnose interference and validate recovery with independent controls.
Design sampling, blanks, standards and calibration for titrimetric and gravimetric analyses; estimate concentration, uncertainty, detection limits and matrix effects.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Biochemistry
decks.description: Explain biological function through molecular structure and energetics.

includes: Biomolecular chemistry, folding, enzyme models and central metabolism

practice: Analyze a metabolic perturbation using molecular structures, stoichiometric balances and enzyme-rate calculations, distinguishing thermodynamic from kinetic control.

outcomes.description: Represent proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates and lipids; explain folding, binding, catalysis and membrane assembly through stereochemistry, noncovalent interactions and free-energy differences.

Use a locally developed steady-state Michaelis-Menten model and inhibition variants to calculate rates; trace carbon, electrons and ATP through glycolysis, respiration, photosynthesis and biosynthetic regulation.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Equilibrium
decks.description: Predict composition and direction of chemical change.

includes: Mass-action equilibrium, acid-base and solubility calculations, reaction energy and redox

practice: Predict a titration curve and precipitation sequence and design an algebraic concentration-cell experiment.

outcomes.description: Calculate reaction enthalpy, Gibbs-energy changes and cell potentials using supplied thermochemical data, ΔG relations and the Nernst equation; explain activity and reversibility limits.
Solve ideal-solution mass-action, mass-balance and charge-balance problems for acids, buffers, complexes and precipitates; test approximations against concentrations.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Kinetics
decks.description: Infer reaction dynamics from concentration-time evidence.

includes: Rate laws, integrated kinetics, temperature dependence and mechanism discrimination

practice: Fit a reaction time course with a stated software optimizer, compare mechanisms and propose a discriminating isotope, concentration or temperature experiment.

outcomes.description: Construct elementary reaction schemes, derive rate laws using pre-equilibrium and steady-state approximations and design perturbations that distinguish competing mechanisms.
Derive and fit zero-, first- and second-order integrated rate laws and Arrhenius relations using concentration or signal data, with residual and uncertainty checks.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Thermodynamics
decks.description: Derive equilibrium and stability in chemical systems.

includes: Chemical potentials, nonideal mixtures, phase equilibria and thermodynamic response

practice: Construct a binary-mixture phase diagram from a free-energy model and infer nonideality parameters from phase-equilibrium data using a provided solver.

outcomes.description: Derive thermodynamic potentials, Maxwell relations, chemical potentials and partial molar quantities; calculate activities and fugacities using specified nonideal models.
Determine reaction and multicomponent phase equilibria, construct phase diagrams and apply Gibbs phase rule and stability criteria with explicit standard-state conventions.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Electrochemistry and Interfaces
decks.description: Connect electrochemical signals to transport and interfacial mechanisms.

includes: Electrode kinetics, diffusion, interfacial charge and electrochemical inverse methods

practice: Analyze a supervised cell or archived electrochemical dataset and distinguish multiple mechanisms through perturbation and residual analysis.

outcomes.description: Interpret voltammetry and impedance data using documented fitting tools, distinguish kinetic, transport and capacitive effects and evaluate corrosion, battery or electrocatalytic design tradeoffs.
Derive bounded Butler-Volmer/Tafel, diffusion-layer and double-layer equivalent-circuit models with stated assumptions; calculate current, overpotential, limiting flux and charging transients.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Electronic Structure Methods
decks.description: Calculate molecular electronic structure with controlled approximations.

includes: Hartree-Fock, density-functional models, correlation, potential-energy surfaces and validation

practice: Implement minimal-basis Hartree-Fock and benchmark a reaction-energy prediction across documented approximation levels without treating software agreement as proof.

outcomes.description: Derive Slater-determinant Hartree-Fock and generalized self-consistent-field equations and implement a small restricted solver using supplied integrals; explain density-functional and perturbative/configuration-interaction correlation approximations.

Use documented electronic-structure tools for geometries, frequencies and reaction paths; distinguish basis, correlation, functional, spin and convergence errors and validate energies and spectra against independent evidence.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Inorganic Chemistry and Catalysis
decks.description: Explain and test inorganic catalytic mechanisms.

includes: Organometallic bonding, catalytic cycles, inorganic mechanisms and spectroscopic discrimination
excludes: Every homogeneous and heterogeneous catalyst class

practice: Construct competing catalytic cycles and design a minimal set of kinetic and spectroscopic experiments that discriminates between them.

outcomes.description: Derive catalytic rate/selectivity models and distinguish resting states and turnover-limiting steps using kinetic, isotope, spectroscopic and poisoning evidence for molecular and surface catalysts.
Construct orbital and electron-count descriptions of metal-ligand bonding and predict oxidative addition, reductive elimination, insertion, elimination and ligand-exchange pathways.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Inorganic Chemistry
decks.description: Explain inorganic structures and reactivity using accessible bonding models.

includes: Main-group chemistry, solids, coordination compounds and qualitative ligand fields

practice: Identify plausible structures and spin states for unknown complexes from stoichiometric, magnetic and reactivity evidence.

outcomes.description: Use explicitly defined crystal-field splitting and high/low-spin rules to predict magnetism and compare ligand substitution, acid-base and redox behavior with their model limitations.
Predict main-group bonding, crystal stoichiometry, coordination geometry and isomerism using periodic trends, lattice models and electron counting.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Laboratory Foundations
decks.description: Produce traceable chemical measurements safely.

includes: Mass and volume measurement, solution preparation, separation, uncertainty and chemical risk

practice: Prepare and recover a benign solute through separation, documenting calibration, uncertainty, waste handling and a comparative risk assessment.

outcomes.description: Compare chemical procedures using exposure, incompatibility, waste and environmental evidence; select controls and justify a safer alternative.
Prepare solutions and perform weighing, volumetric transfer, filtration and recrystallization; calculate uncertainty, recovery and mass balance from a laboratory notebook.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Matter and Reactions
decks.description: Translate between chemical particles, formulas and quantities.

includes: Atoms, periodicity, bonding, molecular geometry and stoichiometry

practice: Identify an unknown reaction stoichiometry from mass and gas-volume data and reconcile symbolic equations with particulate diagrams.

outcomes.description: Use empirical electron-shell, periodic, Lewis, resonance and electron-pair models to predict bonding, polarity and three-dimensional molecular geometry and state their limitations.
Balance reactions and calculate moles, limiting reagents, yields, concentrations and gas quantities with dimensional checks.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Molecular Simulation
decks.description: Sample molecular systems and infer equilibrium properties.

includes: Molecular dynamics, Monte Carlo, molecular force fields and free-energy estimation

practice: Implement a simple molecular fluid and estimate a free-energy difference with replicate trajectories, overlap diagnostics and a force-field sensitivity study.

outcomes.description: Derive free-energy perturbation and umbrella-reweighting estimators, use documented sampling tools and quantify overlap, finite-size, sampling and force-field uncertainties against independent structural or thermodynamic data.

Implement pair forces, periodic boundaries, neighbor lists, velocity-Verlet integration and Metropolis moves; compare ensembles, thermostats, conservation, equilibration and autocorrelation using explicit molecular-coordinate models.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Molecular Spectroscopy
decks.description: Infer molecular structure from complementary spectra.

includes: Working IR, UV-visible, first-order NMR and mass-spectral structure interpretation
excludes: Quantum derivation and multidimensional spin dynamics

practice: Solve blinded unknown structures and justify every assignment, including contradictory peaks and an additional experiment that would resolve ambiguity.

outcomes.description: Apply explicitly taught photon-transition, harmonic-bond, shielding, first-order spin-coupling and ion-fragmentation models to predict simple spectral features and recognize their breakdown.
Combine formula, isotope patterns, IR, UV-visible and one-dimensional proton/carbon NMR evidence to distinguish constitutional and stereochemical hypotheses and identify unresolved structure.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Chemistry
decks.description: Predict and explain transformations of carbon compounds.

includes: Organic structure, stereochemistry, mechanisms and introductory synthesis

practice: Solve a mechanism-and-synthesis portfolio in which each proposed product and route must include competing reactions and stereochemical justification.

outcomes.description: Use electron-pushing and energy diagrams to predict substitution, elimination, addition, aromatic and carbonyl reactions, including competing pathways and stereochemical outcomes.
Translate line, Newman, chair and wedge-dash representations; assign stereochemistry and compare conformational, resonance and acid-base stability.
Design short functional-group syntheses using retrosynthetic disconnections, chemoselectivity and protecting-group logic and identify unsupported selectivity assumptions.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Polymers and Materials
decks.description: Connect chemical structure and processing to material performance.

includes: Polymer synthesis classes, molecular-weight distributions and material characterization
excludes: Electronic band derivations and industrial qualification

practice: Characterize a polymer or composite from supplied and measured data and recommend a material with explicit durability, recyclability and uncertainty considerations.

outcomes.description: Interpret thermal, mechanical, chromatographic and powder-diffraction measurements using locally taught transition, stress-strain and Bragg models; compare polymers, ceramics, glasses and composites and justify lifecycle tradeoffs.
Compare step-growth and chain-growth mechanisms, calculate number/weight-average molecular masses from distributions and relate architecture, crosslinking and tacticity to properties.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Quantum Chemistry
decks.description: Connect quantum states to molecular bonding and spectra.

includes: Molecular orbitals, symmetry, bonding and quantum spectroscopy

practice: Build a small molecular-orbital secular calculation and infer bond length and force constant from rotational-vibrational data.

outcomes.description: Construct Born-Oppenheimer molecular Hamiltonians and linear-combination orbital models; use locally taught point-group operations and character tables to form symmetry-adapted orbitals and calculate simple secular energies.

Derive rigid-rotor and harmonic vibrational spectra and dipole selection rules; calculate rotational/vibrational constants and interpret electronic transitions and ligand-field bonding beyond qualitative models.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Advanced Algorithms
decks.description: Design algorithms with stronger performance guarantees.

includes: Randomized and approximation algorithms, network flow, linear programming and integer formulations

practice: Implement an exact and an approximation approach to a resource-allocation problem and prove bounds independently of empirical benchmarks.

outcomes.description: Design and prove guarantees for randomized, approximation and online algorithms using concentration bounds developed from moment and exponential arguments.
Formulate flow, linear and integer optimization models; derive linear-program duality, implement a bounded simplex solver and use relaxations, rounding and branch-and-bound with certificates or gaps.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Artificial Intelligence
decks.description: Construct agents that search, reason and act under bounded uncertainty.

includes: Heuristic search, planning, constraints, logic and discrete probabilistic inference

practice: Build an agent for a partially uncertain grid environment and compare search and decision policies under explicit model misspecification.

outcomes.description: Construct propositional knowledge bases and discrete Bayesian networks, implement inference by elimination, and solve finite Markov decision processes by value iteration.
Represent states, actions, constraints and goals; implement A*, adversarial search, constraint propagation and finite-state planning with completeness and cost analysis.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Architecture
decks.description: Connect programs to digital hardware execution.

includes: Boolean circuits, instruction sets, memory hierarchy and machine-level programming

practice: Build a small processor in a logic simulator and write an assembly program; separately profile cache-sensitive array traversal.

outcomes.description: Construct Boolean combinational and sequential circuits, represent integers and floating-point numbers, and trace a simple pipelined processor and cache hierarchy.
Translate small C-like programs with pointers, stack frames and heap allocation into assembly; measure locality and diagnose representation or memory errors.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Graphics
decks.description: Construct images from explicit spatial models.

includes: Geometric transformations, projection, rasterization, ray tracing and image sampling
excludes: Continuum simulation and advanced global illumination

practice: Implement a small rasterizer and ray tracer and validate their projections and visibility against analytically constructed scenes.

outcomes.description: Implement ray-object intersections, local reflection models, texture interpolation and antialiasing; distinguish geometric, lighting and sampling artifacts.
Represent meshes and cameras in homogeneous coordinates, compose rigid/projective transformations and implement clipping, visibility and barycentric rasterization.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Networks
decks.description: Explain and implement communication across unreliable networks.

includes: Layered protocols, addressing, routing, reliability and socket programming

practice: Build a file-transfer protocol in an emulated lossy network and compare measured performance with an explicit delay/loss model.

outcomes.description: Implement socket clients and servers and a bounded retransmission protocol; interpret packet captures, congestion behavior and protocol failure cases.
Trace Ethernet, IP, transport, DNS and application exchanges; calculate subnetting, throughput, delay and loss effects and apply locally taught distance-vector/link-state routing procedures.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Cryptography
decks.description: Analyze cryptographic constructions through explicit adversarial definitions.

includes: Security games, reductions, symmetric and public-key constructions

practice: Write a game-based security proof and implement a toy construction solely for testing, then demonstrate why a plausible insecure variant fails.

outcomes.description: Analyze encryption, authenticated encryption, signatures and key exchange based on modular arithmetic and stated hardness assumptions; separate mathematical security from randomness and side-channel failures.
Define indistinguishability, pseudorandomness, unforgeability and computational security and construct reductions between adversarial games with quantified advantage.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Data Structures and Algorithms
decks.description: Design efficient, correct programs over structured data.

includes: Data structures, graph algorithms, algorithm design and complexity

practice: Implement and benchmark a route planner; prove its core invariant and explain adversarial cases rather than relying only on timing.

outcomes.description: Implement sorting, graph traversal, shortest paths and dynamic programming using explicit array, tree or adjacency representations.
Prove loop and recursive correctness, solve runtime recurrences and compare worst-case, average and amortized bounds.
Implement lists, stacks, queues, hash tables, heaps and balanced search-tree operations and compare their invariants and costs.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Databases
decks.description: Design and query reliable persistent information systems.

includes: Relational modeling, SQL, transactions, indexes and retrieval

practice: Build a database-backed document service, demonstrate transaction anomalies and benchmark alternative indexes and query plans.

outcomes.description: Translate information requirements into relational schemas, dependencies and normalized designs; express and compare queries in relational algebra and SQL.
Explain and implement small index, join and transaction mechanisms; compare query plans and construct a text inverted index with an explicitly defined ranking function.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Distributed and Parallel Systems
decks.description: Construct systems that remain correct across concurrency and failures.

includes: Consistency, replication, consensus, fault tolerance and parallel computation

practice: Build a replicated key-value service with fault injection and a parallel data job, reporting consistency evidence and scaling bottlenecks.

outcomes.description: Specify consistency and failure models, reason with logical clocks and implement a bounded replicated log using a taught consensus protocol; analyze partitions, recovery and impossibility assumptions.
Implement shared-memory and message-passing reductions and distributed data processing; analyze work/span, communication, load balance and reproducibility under parallel execution.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Graduate Machine Learning
decks.description: Analyze learning guarantees and advanced representation models.

includes: Statistical learning theory, kernels, latent-variable learning and sequential decision learning

practice: Reproduce a small learning experiment, derive its objective and test a theoretical assumption through controlled distribution shift.

outcomes.description: Derive variational objectives for latent-variable models and implement a variational autoencoder and a finite-state reinforcement learner, teaching Bellman equations, policy gradients and off-policy evaluation assumptions.

Derive generalization bounds using concentration, finite classes and capacity measures; analyze regularization, kernel methods and optimization/generalization tradeoffs under explicit sampling assumptions.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Human-Computer Interaction
decks.description: Design and evaluate interfaces using human evidence.

includes: Interaction design, accessibility, qualitative inquiry and usability experiments

practice: Compare two prototypes using a prespecified study and an accessibility audit, documenting both qualitative findings and quantitative uncertainty.

outcomes.description: Elicit user needs, construct task models and prototypes and evaluate affordances, cognitive load, error recovery and accessibility.
Conduct consent-aware usability studies, code qualitative observations and analyze task outcomes; justify design decisions when convenience, inclusion and privacy conflict.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Languages and Compilers
decks.description: Translate and execute programs through explicit language representations.

includes: Language paradigms, parsing, type checking, intermediate representations and compilation

practice: Implement a compiler for a small typed language and test semantic preservation by differential execution against an interpreter.

outcomes.description: Construct an intermediate representation, implement local dataflow analysis and optimization, and generate stack-machine or assembly code with runtime storage conventions.
Compare imperative, functional and object-based language behavior; implement lexical analysis, recursive-descent or table-driven parsing, scope resolution and a small static type checker.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Machine Learning
decks.description: Construct predictive models and evaluate generalization.

includes: Supervised and unsupervised learning, neural networks, representation and evaluation

practice: Implement a baseline and neural model from explicit objectives, perform ablations and submit a reproducible model card with failure analysis.

outcomes.description: Implement linear classifiers, trees, nearest-neighbor methods, k-means, principal-component analysis and finite-mixture expectation-maximization with explicit objectives and representations.
Design leakage-free training and evaluation, compare calibration and subgroup errors and justify choices involving fairness, interpretability, privacy and deployment shift.
Derive reverse-mode differentiation on computation graphs and implement a small neural network; use convolution, attention and sequence representations in documented image or text models.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Operating Systems
decks.description: Implement and reason about resource-sharing system software.

includes: Processes, virtual memory, filesystems, concurrency and OS interfaces

practice: Extend an instructional kernel and build a concurrent server, using stress tests and invariants to expose scheduling and synchronization defects.

outcomes.description: Use processes, threads, locks, condition variables and atomic operations through taught systems APIs; diagnose races, deadlocks and memory-ordering failures.
Implement bounded scheduler, virtual-memory and filesystem components; explain traps, system calls, page tables, caching and crash recovery.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Programming
decks.description: Construct and test small programs from first principles.

includes: Imperative programming, functions, collections, files and debugging

practice: Implement a command-line data-cleaning application with documented functions, malformed-input handling and automated tests.

outcomes.description: Parse text and tabular files, validate inputs, transform records and produce documented outputs while handling errors.
Trace and write programs using numeric and Boolean expressions, branches, loops, functions, recursion and list/dictionary representations.
Design boundary and example tests, inspect execution state, isolate defects and explain program behavior.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Robotics
decks.description: Connect embodied sensing, inference and action.

includes: Robot kinematics, localization, state estimation, planning and feedback

practice: Implement a mobile-robot localization and navigation pipeline in simulation and test sensor dropout, obstacle uncertainty and controller failure.

outcomes.description: Implement configuration-space collision checking, graph/sampling-based path planning and trajectory feedback; validate estimation consistency, constraints and human-safety failure cases.

Construct planar and three-dimensional rigid-transform kinematics and Jacobians; derive Gaussian linear conditioning and implement Kalman/extended-Kalman localization with sensor and linearization models.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Security Engineering
decks.description: Identify threats and validate proportionate defenses.

includes: Threat modeling, application and network defenses, authentication and authorized assessment

practice: Audit a deliberately vulnerable local service, reproduce authorized failures and deliver tested repairs and a risk-based disclosure report.

outcomes.description: Assess injection, authentication, network and memory-boundary failures in isolated examples; prioritize mitigations and justify authorization, disclosure, privacy and usability decisions.
Construct threat models and implement access control, input validation, secret handling and secure communication using documented cryptographic libraries and explicit trust assumptions.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Semantics and Verification
decks.description: Prove properties of languages and programs.

includes: Operational semantics, type soundness, program logics and model checking

practice: Prove soundness of a small language extension and verify a concurrent protocol using both a hand invariant and an implemented finite-state checker.

outcomes.description: Specify safety/liveness properties, derive Hoare-style proofs and weakest preconditions, and implement finite-state model checking while explaining abstraction and state-explosion limits.
Define small- and big-step semantics and typed lambda-calculus rules; prove substitution, progress and preservation by structural induction.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Software Engineering
decks.description: Deliver maintainable software against explicit requirements.

includes: Requirements, modular design, testing, version control and professional decisions

practice: Develop a small team application with issue tracking, review history, automated tests, a release process and a documented ethical design decision.

outcomes.description: Plan and deliver a reproducible release; justify tradeoffs involving reliability, privacy, accessibility, licensing, maintenance and stakeholder harm.
Translate requirements into interfaces and modular designs, use version control and code review, and construct unit, integration and acceptance tests.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Theory of Computation
decks.description: Determine what computation can express and efficiently solve.

includes: Automata, grammars, Turing machines, reductions and complexity classes

practice: Implement an automaton interpreter and write separate formal proofs of one undecidability reduction and one NP-completeness reduction.

outcomes.description: Construct Turing-machine and problem reductions, prove undecidability and establish NP-completeness while distinguishing decidability from resource bounds.
Construct finite and pushdown automata, regular expressions and context-free grammars; prove language equivalences and nonrecognizability with appropriate methods.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Abstract Algebra
decks.description: Analyze algebraic structure through homomorphisms and quotients.

includes: Groups, actions, rings, ideals, fields and polynomial arithmetic

practice: Classify small algebraic examples, construct explicit quotient maps and prove why selected polynomial quotients are fields.

outcomes.description: Prove and apply subgroup, quotient, isomorphism, group-action and Sylow results to finite groups and symmetry examples.
Calculate in rings and finite fields, use Euclidean algorithms and ideals, and prove factorization and quotient-field claims for integers and polynomial rings.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Advanced PDE Methods
decks.description: Establish and approximate solutions of field equations.

includes: Weak derivatives, Sobolev spaces, energy estimates and finite-difference/finite-element methods

practice: Prove an energy estimate and implement two discretizations with manufactured solutions, mesh refinement and a demonstrated unstable parameter choice.

outcomes.description: Implement finite differences for one- and two-dimensional diffusion/waves and piecewise-linear finite elements for elliptic equations on triangular meshes; analyze consistency, stability, convergence and mesh error.
Define distributions, weak derivatives and Sobolev spaces; derive weak formulations and energy estimates and prove representative elliptic existence/uniqueness and parabolic stability results.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Calculus
decks.description: Calculate and interpret continuous change and accumulation.

includes: Single-variable limits, derivatives, integrals and series

practice: Derive a continuous accumulation model, calculate its predictions and bound the error of a Taylor approximation.

outcomes.description: Evaluate limits and derivatives, justify local linear approximation and solve single-variable rate and optimization problems.
Calculate definite, indefinite and elementary improper integrals using substitution and integration by parts; connect accumulation to the fundamental theorem.
Determine convergence of standard sequences and series and use Taylor expansions with explicit remainder estimates.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Combinatorics and Number Theory
decks.description: Solve advanced finite counting and arithmetic problems.

includes: Enumerative combinatorics, graph structure, divisibility and modular arithmetic

practice: Solve a counting problem by two independent methods and construct an efficient modular computation with a proof of correctness.

outcomes.description: Prove and calculate with divisibility, congruences, the Chinese remainder theorem, Euler/Fermat results and elementary quadratic residues.
Use inclusion-exclusion, generating functions and graph invariants to count structures and prove matching, connectivity and extremal bounds.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Complex Analysis
decks.description: Use the rigidity of complex differentiability.

includes: Holomorphic functions, contour integration, residues and conformal maps

practice: Produce rigorous contour calculations, including vanishing-arc estimates, and map a planar boundary problem to a solvable domain.

outcomes.description: Evaluate real and complex integrals with residues and branch choices; construct elementary conformal maps and use them to solve bounded two-dimensional potential problems.
Prove and apply Cauchy-Riemann, Cauchy integral, power-series and maximum-principle results and classify isolated singularities.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Continuous Optimization
decks.description: Formulate and solve continuous optimization problems.

includes: Smooth and convex optimization, constrained optimality and implementable solvers

practice: Implement constrained least-squares and sparse-estimation solvers and compare numerical stopping criteria with provable optimality certificates.

outcomes.description: Establish convexity, derive first/second-order and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions and use Lagrangian dual bounds under explicit constraint qualifications.
Implement gradient, Newton, projected-gradient and basic proximal methods; derive elementary convergence bounds and diagnose poor scaling and nonconvex failure.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Differential Equations
decks.description: Formulate and solve dynamical models.

includes: First- and second-order ODEs, linear systems and phase portraits

practice: Derive a forced two-state model, solve its linear case and compare phase-portrait predictions with provided numerical trajectories.

outcomes.description: Solve separable and linear first-order equations, constant-coefficient second-order equations and forced linear systems using initial conditions, eigenmodes and matrix exponentials.
Construct phase portraits, locate equilibria, classify local stability by linearization and use existence/uniqueness conditions to interpret one- and two-dimensional models.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Differential Geometry
decks.description: Calculate and prove coordinate-independent geometric relationships.

includes: Smooth manifolds, tensors, differential forms, connections and curvature

practice: Calculate the same curvature invariant in two charts and derive geodesics for a curved surface and a simple Lorentzian metric.

outcomes.description: Calculate metrics, Levi-Civita connections, geodesics and Riemann/Ricci curvature in Riemannian and Lorentzian examples and connect local curvature with geometric invariants.
Construct manifold charts and tangent/cotangent spaces; transform tensor components, calculate exterior derivatives and pullbacks and apply manifold Stokes' theorem.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Dynamics and Control
decks.description: Analyze and control dynamical systems in state space.

includes: Nonlinear dynamics, numerical time integration, feedback and deterministic state estimation

practice: Implement a controlled two-state plant, compare open/closed-loop behavior and demonstrate instability caused by delay or an excessive integration step.

outcomes.description: Construct state-space and transfer-function models, test controllability and observability, and design pole-placement feedback and Luenberger observers with robustness checks.
Analyze stability with Jacobians and Lyapunov functions, identify elementary bifurcations and implement Euler and Runge-Kutta integration with step-size and stability checks.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Functional Analysis
decks.description: Analyze infinite-dimensional linear problems.

includes: Banach/Hilbert spaces, bounded operators, duality and spectral foundations

practice: Prove solvability and stability of an infinite-dimensional variational problem and construct a counterexample when a key hypothesis fails.

outcomes.description: Prove completeness and approximation properties in sequence and function spaces; apply Hahn-Banach, uniform boundedness and open-mapping results and distinguish weak from norm convergence.
Analyze bounded and compact operators, adjoints and spectra; prove Hilbert projection and compact self-adjoint spectral results and apply variational solvability arguments.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Algebra
decks.description: Use structural algebra to classify extensions and representations.

includes: Modules, field extensions, Galois theory and finite-group representations

practice: Determine a nontrivial polynomial's Galois group and decompose a finite-group action into irreducible representations with full justification.

outcomes.description: Prove and apply the Galois correspondence to polynomial solvability and construct finite-group representations and character decompositions over the complex numbers.
Analyze modules over principal ideal domains, exact sequences and tensor products; relate module structure to canonical matrix forms and calculate finite field extensions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Statistics
decks.description: Derive statistical guarantees and perform advanced inference.

includes: Decision and likelihood theory, asymptotic inference, hierarchical Bayes and Monte Carlo

practice: Derive an estimator's limiting law and implement a hierarchical posterior analysis, testing both interval coverage and sampling diagnostics.

outcomes.description: Construct hierarchical Bayesian models and implement importance sampling, Metropolis-Hastings and Gibbs sampling; justify invariant distributions and diagnose convergence and posterior predictive failure.
Analyze sufficiency, information, optimal tests and estimator risk; derive regular likelihood consistency/asymptotic normality and explain failures at boundaries or under misspecification.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Linear Algebra
decks.description: Work with linear transformations and finite-dimensional state spaces.

includes: Real and complex vector spaces, matrices, eigenstructure and least squares

practice: Recover an unknown vector from noisy linear measurements and compare exact, least-squares and rank-truncated solutions.

outcomes.description: Construct projections, least-squares solutions and singular-value decompositions and diagnose rank deficiency.
Solve linear systems by elimination and represent linear maps through bases, rank, null spaces, determinants and coordinate changes.
Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors; use inner products, orthogonal/unitary bases and diagonalization of symmetric or Hermitian matrices.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Measure and Probability
decks.description: Build rigorous integration and probabilistic limit arguments.

includes: Measure, Lebesgue integration, continuous probability and limit theorems

practice: Write a measure-theoretic proof portfolio and analyze convergence of a stochastic sequence with both theorem hypotheses and counterexamples.

outcomes.description: Construct measurable functions and Lebesgue integrals and prove/apply monotone and dominated convergence, product integration and Radon-Nikodym results with explicit hypotheses.

Calculate continuous and joint distributions, conditional expectations and characteristic functions; prove core laws of large numbers and a central limit theorem and analyze elementary Markov chains and martingales.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Multivariable Calculus
decks.description: Calculate with fields and geometry in several dimensions.

includes: Multivariable differentiation, curves, surfaces and vector integration

practice: Represent a three-dimensional field in two coordinate systems and verify an integral theorem on a curved boundary.

outcomes.description: Parametrize curves and surfaces; compute tangent and normal directions, arc length, area and elementary curve and surface curvature.
Calculate gradients, Jacobians, Hessians, total derivatives, constrained extrema and multiple integrals with coordinate changes in two and three dimensions.
Calculate line and surface integrals, divergence, curl and Laplacians in Cartesian, cylindrical and spherical coordinates and apply Green, Gauss and Stokes theorems.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Numerical Computing
decks.description: Implement numerical calculations with defensible error control.

includes: Floating-point error, root finding, interpolation, quadrature and numerical linear algebra

practice: Implement a tested numerical library and construct cases where a small residual conceals a large solution error.

outcomes.description: Implement pivoted elimination and QR least squares, use an SVD library transparently, and diagnose ill-conditioning through residuals and perturbation experiments.
Implement bisection, Newton iteration, polynomial interpolation and composite quadrature; derive elementary error bounds and distinguish conditioning, truncation and roundoff.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Probability and Data
decks.description: Quantify elementary uncertainty and interpret samples.

includes: Finite probability, conditional probability, descriptive statistics and sampling

practice: Analyze a diagnostic-test example and use a spreadsheet sampling experiment to explain base-rate effects and sample-size dependence.

outcomes.description: Summarize data graphically and numerically; distinguish sampling from measurement bias and use a supplied normal model or simulation to describe sampling variability.
Construct finite sample spaces, apply conditional probability and Bayes' rule, and calculate expectations and variances for Bernoulli, binomial and discrete models.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Proof and Discrete Structures
decks.description: Construct proofs and reason with discrete objects.

includes: Logic, sets, relations, induction, graphs and counting

practice: Write a proof portfolio including an induction argument, a graph invariant and a counterexample to a plausible false claim.

outcomes.description: Construct sets, relations, functions, finite graphs and trees; count finite arrangements and solve elementary recurrences.
Translate quantified statements and prove or refute claims using direct proof, contradiction, contraposition and ordinary or structural induction.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Quantitative Foundations
decks.description: Represent quantities and spatial relationships reliably.

includes: Arithmetic, algebra, functions, units, coordinate geometry and complex numbers

practice: Build and check a unit-consistent scaling model from measurements; solve a coordinate-geometry problem using both diagrams and algebra.

outcomes.description: Calculate with fractions, powers, logarithms and units; solve algebraic equations and interpret linear, exponential and trigonometric functions in tables and graphs.
Use Cartesian and polar coordinates, similarity, areas and volumes; calculate with two- and three-dimensional vectors, dot and cross products, and rectangular or polar complex numbers.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Real Analysis
decks.description: Prove the analytical foundations of calculus.

includes: Completeness, metric limits, continuity and convergence of functions

practice: Write complete proofs and counterexamples for a sequence of approximation claims, identifying exactly where uniformity is needed.

outcomes.description: Distinguish pointwise from uniform convergence and prove or refute interchange of limits, derivatives, sums and integrals under explicit hypotheses.
Use completeness, compactness and epsilon-delta arguments to prove sequence, continuity, differentiation and Riemann-integration results on real intervals and metric spaces.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Statistical Inference
decks.description: Make bounded statistical claims from data.

includes: Intervals, tests, simple regression, randomization and study design

practice: Analyze a randomized comparison and an observational dataset, including residual plots, a tool-based bootstrap and a written limits-of-inference statement.

outcomes.description: Calculate and interpret confidence intervals and one- or two-sample tests using normal, t, binomial or randomization procedures; distinguish effect size, uncertainty and multiplicity.
Fit and check simple linear regression using stated formulas or a statistical tool; identify confounding, pseudoreplication and appropriate randomization or blocking.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Statistical Modeling
decks.description: Fit and validate multivariable statistical models.

includes: Multivariate regression, generalized linear models, likelihood and model validation

practice: Build a reproducible regression analysis from raw data, implement resampling and defend the choice of predictive versus causal interpretation.

outcomes.description: Implement bootstrap and permutation procedures, cross-validation and multiple-testing control; diagnose leakage, misspecification, confounding and unstable coefficients.

Construct Gaussian linear, logistic and Poisson models in matrix notation; derive likelihoods and gradients, fit them using a documented optimizer and interpret interactions, regularization and uncertainty.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Topology
decks.description: Reason about shape and continuity independently of coordinates.

includes: Topological spaces, compactness, connectedness, quotients and fundamental groups

practice: Analyze glued polygon models, prove a quotient-space property and calculate a fundamental group using a taught van Kampen procedure.

outcomes.description: Use homotopy, covering-space examples and elementary fundamental-group calculations to distinguish spaces and explain limits of visual intuition.
Construct topologies, subspaces, products and quotients and prove continuity, compactness, connectedness and separation properties.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Transforms and Partial Differential Equations
decks.description: Solve classical field equations in explicit coordinates.

includes: Fourier and Laplace transforms, separation of variables and classical PDE boundary problems

practice: Derive temperature and potential fields in two different geometries and check boundary conditions, dimensions and convergence of truncated expansions.

outcomes.description: Solve heat, wave and Laplace boundary/initial-value problems in intervals, rectangles, cylinders and spheres using separation of variables, locally developed Sturm-Liouville theory and Bessel/Legendre eigenfunctions.
Calculate Fourier series, Fourier/Laplace transforms and convolutions; use orthogonality, eigenfunction expansions and stated convergence conditions to solve forced linear problems.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Analytical Mechanics
decks.description: Derive dynamics from variational and geometric structure.

includes: Variational calculus, Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics, constraints and canonical structure

practice: Derive a constrained multibody system in two coordinate choices and show that its conserved quantities and physical trajectories agree.

outcomes.description: Construct Hamiltonians, calculate Poisson brackets and canonical transformations and analyze rigid-body motion, small oscillations and central-force phase space.
Derive Euler-Lagrange equations from the action, use generalized coordinates and constraints, and connect continuous symmetries to conserved quantities through a taught Noether argument.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Astronomy and Astrophysics
decks.description: Infer astronomical properties from light and motion.

includes: Observational astronomy, stellar properties, galaxies and accessible cosmological models

practice: Analyze an archival light curve and spectrum to infer a stellar or planetary system and report competing parameter explanations.

outcomes.description: Use sky coordinates, parallax, magnitudes, flux, spectral lines, Doppler shifts and transit/light curves to infer distance, temperature, mass, radius and orbital parameters with degeneracy checks.
Apply locally taught blackbody laws, hydrostatic scaling, nuclear-energy bookkeeping and the empirical Hubble relation to explain stellar evolution, galaxies and evidence for dark components.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Circuits and Instruments
decks.description: Analyze circuits and acquire reliable electrical signals.

includes: DC networks, phasor AC models, bounded RC response and basic electronics
excludes: Semiconductor device theory and differential-equation derivation of transients

practice: Build or use a circuit simulator to validate an amplifier and RC filter, then collect calibrated sensor data using a meter and oscilloscope.

outcomes.description: Apply Kirchhoff laws, equivalent circuits and complex impedances to DC and sinusoidal networks; use and interpret a stated exponential RC model, including its initial conditions and limits.
Design a sensor readout with idealized diode, transistor-switch and op-amp models; select grounding, gain, filtering and sampling settings and diagnose loading, clipping and aliasing.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Condensed Matter Physics
decks.description: Predict material behavior from microscopic structure.

includes: Crystals, bands, phonons, transport, magnetism and soft/ordered matter

practice: Derive a lattice dispersion and infer material parameters from diffraction, heat-capacity and conductivity datasets, identifying model failures.

outcomes.description: Calculate lattice normal modes, thermal capacities and Drude transport; analyze bounded spin, elastic and polymer-chain models and interpret evidence for magnetic, liquid-crystalline and superconducting order.

Construct reciprocal lattices and Brillouin zones, derive one-dimensional nearly-free-electron and tight-binding bands and use locally specified Fermi occupation and density-of-states models for metals and semiconductors.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Electromagnetism
decks.description: Calculate electromagnetic fields and their physical effects.

includes: Electrostatics, magnetostatics, material response and Maxwell equations

practice: Solve and compare electrostatic boundary configurations and derive a plane-wave energy balance from Maxwell equations.

outcomes.description: Use integral and differential Maxwell equations to derive induction, field energy and plane-wave propagation; calculate Lorentz-force motion and energy transfer with stated material models.
Calculate fields and potentials from continuous charge/current distributions; apply symmetry, Gauss/Ampere laws and simple conductor/dielectric boundary conditions in three dimensions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Experimental Physics
decks.description: Design and validate an integrated physical measurement.

includes: Instrument integration, signal extraction, parameter inference and experimental judgment

practice: Complete an optical or electromechanical measurement project with a noise budget, independent calibration, reproducible analysis and an uncertainty-supported conclusion.

outcomes.description: Integrate sensors, optics, electronics and data acquisition; teach and implement discrete Fourier analysis, lock-in demodulation and noise spectra with sampling and calibration checks.

Estimate physical parameters using weighted least squares, residuals and a locally taught Jacobian covariance approximation; compare systematic-error models and justify safety, reproducibility and societal-impact decisions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: General Relativity
decks.description: Calculate gravitational phenomena as spacetime dynamics.

includes: Einstein equations, relativistic matter, Schwarzschild geometry and gravitational waves

practice: Derive and compare two observable relativistic corrections and calculate curvature and causal behavior near a Schwarzschild horizon.

outcomes.description: Calculate Schwarzschild redshift, orbit precession, light deflection and horizon properties and derive linearized gravitational-wave propagation and detector strain.
Construct stress-energy tensors for particles and perfect fluids, derive geodesic motion variationally and apply Einstein equations and covariant conservation to symmetric metrics.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Graduate Electrodynamics
decks.description: Solve advanced classical electromagnetic field problems.

includes: Green functions, multipoles, waveguides, radiation and covariant electrodynamics

practice: Derive a waveguide mode and a radiating-source field, verifying boundary conditions, gauge consistency and energy conservation.

outcomes.description: Construct electrostatic Green functions and multipole expansions, solve cylindrical/spherical boundary problems and derive guided-wave and dielectric-interface modes.
Derive retarded potentials and dipole radiation, calculate angular power patterns and express Maxwell equations and field transformations in covariant tensor notation taught locally.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Graduate Quantum Mechanics
decks.description: Solve quantum problems beyond exactly soluble introductory models.

includes: Approximation methods, angular momentum, scattering, density matrices and identical particles

practice: Compare variational and numerical bound-state estimates and calculate a scattering observable, including approximation-validity checks.

outcomes.description: Derive variational, WKB, degenerate and time-dependent perturbation methods; combine angular momenta and derive central-potential radial solutions using a locally developed Frobenius procedure.
Calculate Born and partial-wave scattering, construct bosonic/fermionic many-particle states and density matrices and analyze reduced states, entanglement and measurement statistics.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Mechanics
decks.description: Predict motion and infer forces using Newtonian models.

includes: Calculus-based particle and rigid-body mechanics, conservation and orbits

practice: Derive and test an orbital or rotational model, estimating a physical parameter from measured positions or periods.

outcomes.description: Apply work-energy, momentum and angular momentum conservation to collisions, central-force motion and Kepler orbits; infer force parameters from trajectory data.
Formulate vector Newton equations in Cartesian and plane-polar coordinates; calculate trajectories for integrable forces and rotational motion using torque and moment of inertia.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Modern Physics
decks.description: Interpret evidence that exceeds classical mechanical models.

includes: Special relativity and experimental origins of quantum physics
excludes: General relativity and Schrödinger solution methods

practice: Reconstruct a relativistic collision and estimate physical constants from historical-style photoelectric and spectral data.

outcomes.description: Analyze photoelectric, Compton, atomic-spectrum and matter-wave evidence using photon and de Broglie relations, distinguishing successful predictions from semiclassical model limitations.
Calculate Lorentz transformations, spacetime intervals, four-momentum conservation and relativistic collision thresholds using an explicitly defined Minkowski metric.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics
decks.description: Connect subatomic models to reaction and detector observations.

includes: Nuclear structure, decay, reactions, particle classification and detector evidence
excludes: Field-theoretic scattering derivations and radiation-handling credentials

practice: Reconstruct a resonance from simulated detector events and audit energy thresholds, detector efficiency and alternative background explanations.

outcomes.description: Calculate binding energies, decay chains, tunneling estimates and reaction Q-values using liquid-drop, shell and barrier models; distinguish fission, fusion and decay mechanisms.

Apply conservation laws, relativistic invariant masses and cross-section definitions to particle reactions; interpret tracking, calorimetry and counting data using locally taught efficiency, Poisson-count and background models.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Optics
decks.description: Build optical predictions and infer object properties from light.

includes: Geometric optics, scalar interference, diffraction models and optical measurement

practice: Construct a lens or grating measurement and estimate an unknown focal length or wavelength with uncertainty and alignment checks.

outcomes.description: Use locally defined sinusoidal phase addition, two-slit, grating and aperture formulas to calculate interference, resolution and polarization intensity; infer wavelength or size and identify model limits.
Construct ray diagrams and calculate imaging, magnification, reflection, refraction and simple lens-system performance with paraxial assumptions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Oscillations and Waves
decks.description: Predict oscillatory and propagating physical disturbances.

includes: Oscillators, normal modes, mechanical waves, acoustics and dispersion

practice: Measure resonances in a coupled oscillator or acoustic tube and infer damping and wave speed from amplitude and phase data.

outcomes.description: Derive and solve damped, driven and coupled oscillator equations; calculate resonance, phase and normal modes from mechanical parameters.

Derive the one-dimensional string or acoustic wave equation from force and continuity balances, verify traveling and standing solutions and calculate impedance, reflection, dispersion and energy flux.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Physical Foundations
decks.description: Build and test elementary physical models.

includes: Units, free-body diagrams, constant-acceleration motion, energy and measurement

practice: Measure a rolling or falling object's motion, calibrate the measurement method and justify whether discrepancies exceed measurement uncertainty.

outcomes.description: Measure length, time, mass and motion; estimate resolution and repeatability, propagate simple independent uncertainties and compare evidence with a model.
Construct free-body diagrams and use algebraic force, pressure, constant-acceleration, momentum and energy models in one and two dimensions.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Mechanics
decks.description: Calculate predictions from quantum states and observables.

includes: Wavefunctions, operators, finite-state systems, one-dimensional potentials and atomic states
excludes: Full scattering theory and many-body approximations

practice: Calculate transmission through a one-dimensional barrier and spin-sequence probabilities, checking normalization, limiting cases and measurement interpretation.

outcomes.description: Solve one-dimensional wells, barriers and harmonic oscillators; calculate spin measurements, commutators and first-order perturbations and use supplied hydrogen eigenfunctions to interpret three-dimensional atomic quantum numbers.
Normalize complex wavefunctions, calculate continuous probability densities and expectation integrals, use bra-ket notation and Hermitian operators and evolve finite-dimensional states unitarily.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Statistical Physics
decks.description: Analyze quantum populations and collective thermal behavior.

includes: Grand ensembles, quantum gases, interacting models and phase transitions

practice: Compare a simulated spin-model transition with mean-field predictions and calculate a quantum-gas thermodynamic curve with numerical error control.

outcomes.description: Derive mean-field and Landau descriptions of ordering, analyze correlations and critical scaling and implement Metropolis sampling with detailed-balance and finite-size checks.
Derive grand-canonical Bose and Fermi occupations from state counting; calculate blackbody, degenerate-gas and Bose-condensation observables and thermodynamic limits.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Statistical Mechanics
decks.description: Derive macroscopic behavior from microscopic classical models.

includes: Classical ensembles, partition functions, fluctuations and transport models

practice: Derive thermodynamic predictions for a classical model and compare fluctuation or diffusion measurements with the model's microscopic assumptions.

outcomes.description: Construct microcanonical and canonical ensembles, derive Boltzmann weights and partition-function relations and calculate ideal-gas, oscillator and discrete-spin thermodynamics.
Calculate fluctuations, correlations and response; derive Maxwell velocity distributions and bounded random-walk and kinetic-theory estimates for diffusion and transport.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Stellar and Cosmological Physics
decks.description: Build quantitative models of stars and cosmic expansion.

includes: Stellar structure, radiative transfer, compact objects and quantitative cosmology

practice: Implement a stellar-structure shooting calculation and compare expansion-distance predictions with an archival dataset using a supplied least-squares tool.

outcomes.description: Use explicitly stated Friedmann equations and matter/radiation equations of state to calculate expansion histories, distances and horizons; fit bounded cosmological models and assess parameter degeneracies without claiming an Einstein-equation derivation.

Derive and numerically integrate spherical stellar mass, pressure, luminosity and temperature equations using stated opacity and nuclear-rate models; solve one-dimensional radiative transfer and analyze degenerate support.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Thermal Physics
decks.description: Analyze macroscopic thermal processes.

includes: Temperature, heat, equations of state, thermodynamic laws and heat engines

practice: Reconstruct an engine cycle from pressure-volume data and audit a thermal-efficiency claim against energy and entropy balances.

outcomes.description: Calculate entropy changes and engine or refrigerator performance from reversible reference paths; diagnose irreversibility and distinguish state from path quantities.
Calculate heat, work and internal-energy changes for ideal gases, calorimetry, phase changes and elementary conduction using stated constitutive laws.

coverage.subject: computer-science
coverage.rationale: Provides spatial rendering and empirical human-centered design, including accessibility and consent decisions.

coverage.subject: computer-science
coverage.rationale: Develops implementation-level systems, translation, security engineering and predictive learning.

coverage.subject: computer-science

scopeIssues: Physics: established working fluid mechanics and its advanced continuum continuation remain unfinished. Pressure, flow and diffusion applications appear in physical foundations, physiology, waves and statistical mechanics, but no contract teaches deriving and solving viscous incompressible flow or validating a fluid experiment. These neighboring outcomes do not provide full undergraduate-advanced fluid-mechanics coverage.

Physics: established plasma-physics foundations remain unfinished. Electromagnetism and statistical mechanics do not teach charged-fluid or kinetic plasma models, Debye screening, plasma oscillations and magnetized transport as a coherent graduate capability.

Chemistry: established graduate molecular spectroscopy remains unfinished. The included chemistry/molecular-spectroscopy outcomes provide working first-order interpretation and chemistry/quantum-chemistry provides basic quantum spectra, but no contract teaches multidimensional NMR pulse-sequence reasoning or time-resolved molecular spectroscopic inference at graduate depth.

Mathematics: linear programming has a teaching contract in computer-science/advanced-algorithms, but its only route imposes the complete advanced-algorithm curriculum rather than an independent undergraduate working entry. An accessible linear/discrete optimization route remains to be separated while preserving the graduate guarantees.
practiceNotes: Retrieval practice should maintain definitions, representations, assumptions, diagnostic distinctions and method selection; it does not certify proof-writing, programming, laboratory technique or field competence.
Assess extended work separately using unseen problems, reproducible code, laboratory notebooks, raw data, uncertainty analysis, oral defense and revision after feedback.

Laboratory and field projects require suitable facilities, training, supervision and local risk assessment. Use nonpathogenic organisms, low-energy apparatus and safer chemical substitutions where possible.

Human-participant work, identifiable biological data, animal research, genetic interventions and environmental sampling require applicable consent, ethics review and permissions; these are not assumed available.
Security exercises require explicit authorization and isolated systems. Public datasets and synthetic environments can replace unavailable production infrastructure.
Provided scientific software may be used only where a contract says to use it; implementation and proof outcomes require the learner's own algorithmic work.
Clinical interpretation, hazardous synthesis, radiation handling and regulated professional practice are not authorized by completing these decks.
